prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an upward-angled indoor room with a foreground clothing rack at the bottom left (~0.5–1.0 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach), a person in a baseball cap standing just behind the rack (~1.2–1.8 m away, within arm's reach of the rack), a second clothing rack slightly further right and behind the first (~2.0–2.5 m away), an overhead rectangular light fixture above (~2.5–3.0 m away), and a windowed back wall ~3.5–4.5 m behind the foreground. Across the five frames, the person behind the foreground rack shifts slightly rightward relative to the rack's vertical post while turning their head clockwise from facing right in frames 1–3 to facing and looking directly toward the camera wearer in frame 5, emerging from heavy occlusion behind the hangers. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the depth planes of the foreground rack, the person's head immediately behind it, the secondary rack, and the back wall even where dark clothing and hangers visually blend together. However, the map is unreliable where bright white depth values bleed across the gaps between hangers onto the person's lower face and neck in frames 1–4, and where the transparent exterior windows are rendered at the same flat depth as the interior wall frames.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map fails to detect the person in frames 1 and 3 and detects no non-person objects (such as the clothing racks, hangers, ceiling lights, or windows) in any frame, showing only isolated 'person' masks in the lower portion of frames 2, 4, and 5. In frame 2, a pink 'person' mask captures the person's capped head and neck (~1.5 m away, just behind the foreground rack at bottom center-left), broken into fragments by the occluding foreground rack bar and hangers. In frame 4, as the person turns toward the camera wearer, the map outputs overlapping pink and brown 'person' masks that merge the person's head with the foreground rack to the left, plus a small cyan 'person' mask on a hanging garment on the right rack (~2.0–2.5 m away). In frame 5, when the person faces the camera wearer to the right of the foreground rack post, a single pink 'person' mask covers their head and shoulders but erroneously extends leftward along the foreground clothing rack (~0.5–1.0 m away, within arm's reach). While segmentation helps locate the partially occluded person amidst cluttered hangers in frames 2, 4, and 5, it is highly unreliable due to complete false negatives in frames 1 and 3, false-positive 'person' labels on clothing and racks, and merged masks across distinct depth planes.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank in frames 1, 2, 3, and 5, and detects only a minimal four-keypoint yellow upper-body/head skeleton in the lower-left region of frame 4, with no magenta hand skeletons visible in any frame. In frame 4, the sparse yellow keypoints mark the head and right shoulder of the person standing ~1.2–1.8 m in front of the camera wearer just behind the foreground clothing rack, aligning with the moment their head turns from facing right toward the camera wearer. Because the camera points upward and the foreground clothing rack at the bottom edge (~0.5–1.0 m away) occludes the person's torso and arms below the neck, both the camera wearer's own body and the other person's lower body and hands remain entirely out of view or occluded across all five frames. Although the single detection in frame 4 roughly indicates the head-to-shoulder orientation behind the rack, the pose map adds almost no spatial information beyond RGB and is largely unreliable, missing the person entirely in four of the five frames—even in frame 5 where their face and glasses are clearly visible looking directly at the camera wearer.
